text:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: Possible tenant isolation violation detected for tenant ACME_CORP in Dedicated Pool dp-22. Routing anomaly score spike + KV cache correlation. Pager sent to #incidents.

sre_oncall_mike: Acked. I'm exploring now — switching pager to me. @anna_eng can you join?

anna_eng: On it. I see a small set of requests with headers referencing acme-vpc subnet that landed on dp-22 nodes that are usually pinned to acme-priv. Looks like a recent routing label change at 07:12 UTC.

kevin_platform: Flagging: we deployed route-label rewrite in ded-router service at 07:10 for autoscaling test. Rolling back now.

anna_eng: Patch revert in progress: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/ded-router --to-revision=6`

incident-bot: Deploy bot: rollout undo started for ded-router (deploy/ded-router) by kevin_platform.

sre_oncall_mike: Good. While that rolls, let's isolate suspect nodes: dp-22-n{3,4} — short firewall ACL and iptables DROP on inter-tenant traffic.

anna_eng: Running remote commands: 
```ssh root@dp-22-n3
iptables -I FORWARD -s 10.240.32.0/20 -d 10.241.0.0/20 -j DROP
iptables-save | tail -n 20
```

anna_eng: ACLs applied, verified `DROP` rules present.

kevin_platform: Reverted router commit pushed. Routing tables now reflect tenant pins. Confirming no new cross-tenant connections are being accepted.

julie_cust-success: @sre_oncall_mike I'll notify ACME primary contact (ops@acme). Do we have an ETA for impact assessment and customer-facing blurb?

sre_oncall_mike: Short answer: we need to determine if any PII or request bodies were served cross-tenant. Initial trace shows 132 requests with cross-tenant headers between 07:10 and 07:18. We'll run a query against request logs and kv-access logs.

security-bot: Running quick index scan for potential sensitive patterns (SSN/email/creditcard) in captured payloads — this is automated but may return false positives.

anna_eng: Querying logs: `SELECT request_id, src_tenant, dst_tenant, timestamp, path FROM prod.requests WHERE dst_tenant='ACME_CORP' AND src_tenant!='ACME_CORP' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-11-14T07:00:00Z' AND '2026-11-14T07:30:00Z' LIMIT 500;`

anna_eng: Sample output: 
```request_id: r_8f3a, src_tenant: common-analytics, dst_tenant: ACME_CORP, path: /v1/generate, timestamp: 2026-11-14T07:12:04Z
request_id: r_8f4b, src_tenant: test-tenant-7, dst_tenant: ACME_CORP, path: /v1/embeddings, timestamp: 2026-11-14T07:12:19Z
... total matched: 132
```

sre_oncall_mike: Important: are any of these requests carrying user-provided content in bodies? Anna?

anna_eng: Pulling request bodies for a sample set now (redaction tooling engaged). Running `redact-sample --ids r_8f3a,r_8f4b --rules basic`

anna_eng: Redaction shows request bodies are mostly short prompts and metadata. Security bot flagged 2 samples containing plain email addresses in prompts. No large blobs or files.

security-bot: Scanned the 132 captured payloads: 2 suspected sensitive items (email addresses), severity: medium, confidence: low. No SSNs or credit-card-like patterns.

kevin_platform: Given the timeframe and count, exposure window ~= 8 minutes. We'll treat this as sensitive and notify per enterprise SLA while we continue investigation.

julie_cust-success: Draft for ACME (sensitive): "We detected a short-lived routing misconfiguration impacting your Dedicated Pool dp-22 between 07:10-07:18 UTC. A subset of service requests were routed incorrectly to other internal pools. We are investigating and will follow up with details and mitigation steps. No conclusive evidence of high-risk data exposure yet." Thoughts?

sre_oncall_mike: Good. Add: we have quarantined nodes and rolled back the routing change. We're running a full audit across logs and will provide a list of affected request IDs. Also include dedicated incident channel invite and contact escalation path.

anna_eng: Running full audit query to enumerate affected request IDs and potential recipients: `python scripts/audit_tenant_isolation.py --tenant ACME_CORP --pool dp-22 --since 2026-11-14T07:00:00Z --until 2026-11-14T07:30:00Z > /tmp/acme-exposed-132.json`

anna_eng: Dropping sample of JSON (redacted) into the secure share: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/expose-audit/1789123456 (internal link)

kevin_platform: Also confirming control plane logs: ded-router user agent shows a configuration push from devops:ci-runner at 07:09:58 UTC, commit id `b7c6f2`. Tagging config owner: @devops-bot.

incident-bot: Pager: escalation to SRE Lead in 10m if not resolved.

sre_oncall_mike: I'm going to start an immediate post-incident packet capture on dp-22 hosts for forensic sweep: `tcpdump -w /var/log/pcaps/dp22-07-12.pcap host 10.241.0.0/16` (will upload to secure forensic store).

security-bot: Forensics: enable write-protected copy and checksum. Also capturing KV cache get/set keys for timeframe. Running `kv-audit --tenant ACME_CORP --range 07:00-07:30 > /tmp/kv-dump-acme.json`

julie_cust-success: I've sent initial notification to ACME ops with the draft and invited them to a bridge at :30. They asked for estimated scope — I told them we're treating it as limited but tracing every request.

anna_eng: Quick note: no autoscaling events happened during window; weirdly the route label rewrite had a bug that matched on partial pool names (dp-2 matched dp-22). Root cause hypothesis: rewrite used `contains` instead of `equals`.

kevin_platform: Confirmed. Fixing unit tests to assert exact-match. Pushing guard: `if (label === desiredLabel)` + add e2e.

sre_oncall_mike: Next steps:
- finish full request audit and attach list to incident record
- provide customer-facing timeline + mitigations (Julie)
- security to run payload DPI and escalate if sensitive data confirmed (Security)
- platform to add guardrails and revert dangerous rewrite logic (Kevin)
- schedule postmortem and root cause analysis (SRE lead)

security-bot: I'll queue a deeper content analysis against the full set. If confidence > 0.8 for any high-sensitive pattern, auto-escalate to Incident Response.

anna_eng: Audit finished. Uploading redacted CSV with 132 rows to secure storage `/secure/incidents/1789123456/acme_exposed.csv` and attaching SHA256: `3f7d2b9a...`

kevin_platform: Added a network policy unit test and deployed hotfix to ded-router, plus a deploy-time lint rule to disallow substring matching for tenant labels.

julie_cust-success: ACME bridge done. They confirmed seeing 2 anomalous requests (same as we found) — they want copy of the affected request IDs and assurance we're rotating any keys that might have been sent. We need to confirm if API keys appeared in bodies/headers.

anna_eng: Scanned headers from the sample set: no API-key header values leaked. One sample had an API key in the payload (user-supplied) — per customer policy, we recommended they rotate that key. Not a platform secret.

sre_oncall_mike: Handoff: my shift ends in 20m. @anna_eng you're primary for followups; @kevin_platform please own the remediation and CL/PR for the ded-router fix; @security-bot continue DPI. I'll create the incident record and set severity P1 -> P1 (active) until postmortem closes.

anna_eng: Acknowledged. Starting 1h follow-up window and scheduling detailed RCA meeting tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident update: severity=P1, status=mitigated, start=2026-11-14T07:10:00Z, mitigated=2026-11-14T07:18:00Z, followup_channel=#incidents-1789123456.

sre_oncall_mike: Final note for handoff: we've quarantined dp-22-n3/n4, reverted routing, firewall rules in place, audit completed (132 requests, 2 low-confidence email hits). Security says not high-risk at this point but to treat as sensitive. If anything new pops up ping me directly.

julie_cust-success: I'll keep ACME informed and send post-incident comms once we have the RCA. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

security-bot: Added ticket to IR queue IR-2026-0719 for extended analysis.

kevin_platform: I'll publish the hotfix and add the e2e tests. Also adding a deploy guard to block label rewrites without exact-match ops.

anna_eng: Closing thread for now; will reopen if new findings surface.

sre_oncall_mike: Thanks everyone. Handoff complete.
